title: Vitamin D exposures reported to US poison centers 2000-2014: Temporal trends and outcomes
authors: Spiller HA, Good TF, Spiller NE, Aleguas A
population: Single-substance human vitamin D exposures reported to the US National Poison Data System; multivitamin products excluded
funder: not stated in the abstract; the full text was not accessible (HTTP 403 at the publisher), so the funding statement was not read.
result: 25,397 human exposures; a mean of 196 per year in 2000 to 2005 rose by 1600% to a mean of 4535 per year after 2011; median age 10 years. No fatalities; five (0.02%) major-effect outcomes; serious medical outcomes ranged from 2 to 22 patients per year. Clinical effects were mainly gastrointestinal (0.7% to 1.5%) and mild neurological (0.2% to 0.4%).
